newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold, silver end higher on firm world trend.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold, silver end higher on firm world trend.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed five rupees higher at 4,805 rupees per 10 grammes but down from the day's opening of 4,815 rupees.
** Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 grammes) closed steady at 56,200 rupees but were 100 rupees lower compared to the opening of 56,300 rupees as profit-taking trimmed early gains by close.
** Silver (.999) closed 30 rupees higher at 7,450 rupees per kg on limited arrivals and an uptrend in the world market.
Gold 24 carat closed five rupees higher at 4,805 rupees per 10 grammes on limited , dealers said.

Gold was down 20 rupees per 10 grammes on Thursday. Gold opened 15 rupees higher at 4,815 rupees per 10 grammes following a firm trend in the world market before light profit-taking trimmed the early gains. Gold was down 20 rupees per 10 grammes on Thursday.
Prices of gold biscuits (116.50 grammes each) closed steady at 56,200 rupees after opening 100 rupees higher at 56,300 rupees. They were down 200 rupees per piece on Thursday.
Dealers said gold was firm in early trade but dropped towards close on reports that premium on special licences to import gold had fallen 2.0 percent to 11 percent.
"A lower premium has led to lower import costs," said a dealer.
Dealers said the cost of imported gold includes a premium to acquire a special import licence, a duty of 220 rupees per 10 grammes on arrival and local taxes.
Silver (.999) closed 30 rupees higher at 7,450 rupees per kg on limited arrivals and a shortage of ready stock.
Silver opened firm on limited arrivals but sluggish industrial buying trimmed some of the early gains towards close, dealers said.
Silver was down 30 rupees per kg on Thursday.
Market sentiment was subdued at close and traders were expecting sluggish physical demand and a fall in prices next week. (Conversion $1=35.86 rupees)
